key_insight: FineCog-Nav applies a top-down, human-inspired cognitive architecture that decomposes UAV vision-language navigation into fine-grained, interoperable modules, enabling robust zero-shot multimodal navigation without heavy task-specific finetuning. The coordinated module interfaces (language, perception, planning, control) improve grounding and long-horizon instruction execution.
problem_solved: Addresses the limitations of existing zero-shot UAV VLN methods that rely on monolithic large models, generic prompts, and loosely coordinated components—leading to poor grounding, low interpretability, and weak generalization in complex 3D egocentric environments.
method: Top-down modular design: split navigation into specialized cognitive modules (e.g., language parser, semantic perception, short-/long-horizon planner, and action controller) inspired by human cognition.

Structured cross-module interfaces: exchange grounded representations (scene graphs, goal tokens, attentional maps) and explicit communication protocols to align language and perception without end-to-end finetuning.

Lightweight multimodal adapters and rule-based grounding: combine pretrained vision/language encoders with small adapters and symbolic grounding rules to enable zero-shot generalization in novel environments.
impact: FineCog-Nav provides a practical blueprint for building interpretable, sample-efficient VLN systems that generalize zero-shot—reducing dependence on massive task-specific datasets or models and accelerating deployment of reliable autonomous UAV navigation in real-world settings.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing the top-down cognitive modules (Language → Perception → Planner → Controller) and their structured interfaces.

paper_title: FineCog-Nav: Integrating Fine-grained Cognitive Modules for Zero-shot Multimodal UAV Navigation
paper_authors: Dian Shao, Zhengzheng Xu, Peiyang Wang, Like Liu, Yule Wang
